tickets.summary: Failed: “Hide All” button gets disabled after multiple double-clicks on expanded KPI graph (Global/UE Statistics).
tickets.description:
**Step 1:** Log in to Simnovator.

**Step 2:** Navigate to the **Global Statistics** or **UE Statistics** page. From the top-left **Test Case** search bar, select any previously executed multi-cell test case along with the appropriate execution time. The selected test case data will load.

**Step 3:** Perform either of the following actions:

·        From **UE Statistics**, click on any IMSI. It will redirect to the respective UE ID’s KPI page.  
**OR**

·        From the **Global Statistics** KPI section, expand any KPI graph (e.g., Throughput, Packets/Sec, Scheduled UE).

**Step 4:** Ensure the KPI graph is expanded, and Series Control options are visible.

**Step 5:** In the expanded graph view, navigate to **Series Control** and click on **“Hide All.”** This will hide all cell parameters.

**Step 6:** Double-click two to three times within the graph area.

tickets.summary: Failed: “Hide All” button gets disabled after zoom-in (drag right) action on expanded KPI graph.
tickets.description:
**Step 1:** Log in to Simnovator.

**Step 3:** Perform either of the following actions:

* From **UE Statistics**, click on any IMSI. It will redirect to the respective UE ID’s KPI page.  
  **OR**
* From the **Global Statistics** KPI section, expand any KPI graph (e.g., Throughput, Packets/Sec, Scheduled UE).

tickets.summary: Users are unable to create test cases with mobility enabled when configuring two or more cells.
tickets.description:
While creating an test case with mobility enabled and two or more cells configured, the test case creation fails and the user is blocked from proceeding. The following validation errors are observed:

\[CellsConfig\] "Position (X,Y)": expected array, but got null for SA profile 1  
\[CellsConfig\] "Antenna Type": expected string, but got null for SA profile 1

tickets.summary: Failed: Mandatory field validation not applied for User plane parameters based on selected data type.
tickets.description:
**Step1:** Log in to Simnovator.

**Step2:** Click **+ Create Test Case** from the top-right corner and navigate to the **Cell** page.

**Step3:** Enter the required details in the **Cell** and **Subscriber** sections.

**Step4:** Navigate to the **User Plane** section.

**Step5:** From the **Data Type** dropdown, select each available data type one by one.

**Step6:** Verify the mandatory field validation for the parameters associated with each selected data type.

**Step7:** Observe that the expected mandatory fields are not consistently enforced based on the selected data type.

‌

**Acceptance Criteria**

·        **Ping**

o   Destination IP Address must be mandatory.

·        **iPerf**

o   Destination IP Address must be mandatory.

·        **HTTP**

o   URL must be mandatory.

o   Destination IP Address must be mandatory.

o   Transport Protocol must not be mandatory.

·        **VoNR / ViNR**

o   P-CSCF IP Address must be mandatory.

o   APN Name must be mandatory.

·        **FTP**

o   Destination IP Address must be mandatory.

o   File to Upload must be mandatory.

o   File to Download must be mandatory.

o   Username and Password must be mandatory when Anonymous User is disabled.

·        **RTSP**

o   Destination IP Address must be mandatory.

o   File to Download must be mandatory.

·        Appropriate validation messages should be displayed whenever a required field is left empty.

·        Users should not be allowed to save or proceed until all mandatory fields for the selected data type are provided.

·        Mandatory field validation should update dynamically whenever the Data Type selection changes.

tickets.summary: UserPlane Configuration Data Is Lost After Validation Failure When Multiple UserPlanes Are Configured
tickets.description:
While creating a test case with multiple UserPlane configurations, I observed that the data entered in **UserPlane 1** is lost after a validation failure.

In the observed scenario:

1. UserPlane 1 was created with **FTP** as the Data Type, and all mandatory fields were populated.
2. A second UserPlane (UserPlane 2) was created with **VoNR** as the Data Type, and its mandatory fields were also populated.
3. Upon clicking **Next**, a validation popup appeared indicating that some mandatory fields were missing.
4. After returning to UserPlane 1 to verify the configuration, the previously entered FTP details were no longer present.

This behavior results in loss of user-entered configuration data and requires the user to re-enter the details.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Create a new test case.
2. Navigate to the UserPlane configuration section.
3. Create **UserPlane 1** with **FTP** Data Type.
4. Fill all mandatory FTP fields.
5. Create **UserPlane 2** with **VoNR** Data Type.
6. Fill all mandatory VoNR fields.
7. Click **Next**.
8. Observe the validation popup indicating missing mandatory fields.
9. Return to UserPlane 1 and check the previously entered values.  

    ![](blob:https://media.staging.atl-paas.net/?type=file&localId=a9c47d2e73d7&id=cb357ad2-4019-4d8d-96fa-514c1a8f614c&&collection=&height=938&occurrenceKey=null&width=1916&__contextId=null&__displayType=null&__external=false&__fileMimeType=null&__fileName=null&__fileSize=null&__mediaTraceId=null&url=null)

### Expected Result

* Validation should accurately identify the missing mandatory fields.
* Previously entered UserPlane configurations should be retained after validation failure.
* UserPlane 1 and UserPlane 2 data should persist when navigating between configurations.
* No configured data should be lost unless explicitly cleared by the user.

tickets.summary: Missing validation for Number of Packets based on Duration and Interval in Ping User Plane configuration
tickets.description:
When configuring a Ping User Plane test, the application allows users to proceed with an invalid combination of **Duration**, **Interval**, and **Number of Packets**.

For example:

* Duration = **600 sec**
* Interval = **20 sec**
* Number of Packets = **600**

Based on the configured interval, only **30 packets** can be transmitted within 600 seconds. Despite this, the GUI allows the user to click **Next** without displaying any validation error.

The application should validate the relationship between **Duration**, **Interval**, and **Number of Packets** before allowing the user to continue.  

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Navigate to **Create Test Case → User Plane**.
2. Select **Data Type = Ping**.
3. Enter:

    * Packet Size = 56
    * Duration = 600
    * Interval = 20
    * Number of Packets = 600
    
4. Click **Next**.

### Actual Result

The application allows navigation to the next step without validating the entered values.

### Expected Result

The application should validate the configuration and prevent navigation if the **Number of Packets** exceeds the maximum allowed based on the configured **Duration** and **Interval**. An appropriate validation message should be displayed to the user.

tickets.summary: Changing the cell type from FDD to TDD after navigating back results in a JSON unmarshal error.
tickets.description:
While creating a test case, changing the cell type from **FDD** to **TDD** after navigating back from the next page results in a backend JSON parsing error. The application does not correctly handle the previously entered cell configuration, preventing the user from proceeding.

**Steps to Reproduce:**

1. Create a new test case.
2. Navigate to the **Cell** section RAT type 5G.
3. Select **FDD** as the cell type.
4. Enter valid values for **Band**, **Bandwidth**, and other mandatory fields.
5. Click **Next**.
6. Click **Previous** to return to the Cell section.
7. Change the cell type from **FDD** to **TDD**.
8. Click **Next**.

**Observed Result:**  
The following error is displayed:

```
[json] cannot unmarshal number into Go struct field PayloadCell.cells.bandwidth of type string
```

The user cannot proceed to the next step.

**Expected Result:**  
 The application should correctly update the cell configuration when the cell type is changed. Previously entered values should either be revalidated, reset, or converted as required, and the user should be able to continue without any backend parsing errors.

tickets.summary: Next button is not enabled for TUAK algorithm after entering mandatory fields
tickets.description:
While creating a test case in the **Subscriber** section, an issue is observed with the validation of the **TUAK** algorithm.

When **Algorithm = TUAK** is selected and the required **Keccak_f Iterations** value is entered, the **Next** button is not enabled, preventing the user from proceeding.

As a workaround, changing the configuration from **TOPc** to **TOP** enables the **Next** button, allowing the user to proceed. After navigating to the next page and returning to the **Subscriber** section, changing the selection between **TOPc** and **TOP** works as expected, and the **Next** button is enabled correctly.

This indicates that the initial validation for the TUAK algorithm is not triggered correctly and only works after the TOP/TOPc option is changed.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Create a new test case.
2. Navigate to the **Subscriber** section.
3. Select **Algorithm = TUAK**.
4. Enter a valid **Keccak_f Iterations** value.
5. Observe that the **Next** button is not enabled.
6. Change the selection from **TOPc** to **TOP**.
7. Observe that the **Next** button becomes enabled.
8. Navigate to the next page and click **Previous** to return to the Subscriber section.
9. Change the selection between **TOPc** and **TOP** again.

### Observed Result

Initially, the **Next** button is not enabled even after entering all the required values for the TUAK algorithm. It becomes enabled only after toggling the **TOP/TOPc** selection. After navigating back, switching between **TOPc** and **TOP** works correctly.

### Expected Result

When all mandatory fields for the **TUAK** algorithm, including **Keccak_f Iterations**, are configured correctly, the **Next** button should be enabled immediately without requiring the user to toggle between **TOP** and **TOPc**.

![](blob:https://media.staging.atl-paas.net/?type=file&localId=c582f80cccf2&id=f341d446-fdf4-46ec-8d05-20afd3782136&&collection=&height=952&occurrenceKey=null&width=1918&__contextId=null&__displayType=null&__external=false&__fileMimeType=null&__fileName=null&__fileSize=null&__mediaTraceId=null&url=null)

I observed that in the **Subscriber** section, the **SQN** field accepts all letters, numbers, and special characters without any validation. However, the SQN value should be a valid **hexadecimal** value and should only allow characters **0-9, A-F, and a-f**.

**Steps to Reproduce:**

1. Navigate to the **Subscriber** section.
2. Enter invalid characters (e.g., G, Z, @, #, xyz) in the **SQN** field.
3. Observe that the field accepts the invalid input.

**Actual Result:**  
The SQN field accepts non-hexadecimal characters.

**Expected Result:**  
The SQN field should accept only valid hexadecimal characters (**0-9, A-F, a-f**). Invalid characters should be rejected, or an appropriate validation message should be displayed.

tickets.description:

tickets.summary: Subscriber RES Len field accepts invalid values
tickets.description:
**Steps to Reproduce:**

1. Open the application and create a new test case.
2. Navigate to the **Subscriber** section.
3. Configure the required subscriber details.
4. Locate the **RES Len** field (default value is **8**).
5. Replace the value **8** with **128**.
6. Complete any other mandatory fields if required.
7. Click the **Next** button.

**Actual Result:**  
The application accepts the value **128** in the **RES Len** field and allows the user to proceed to the next step without any validation.

**Expected Result:**  
The **RES Len** field should accept only **4**, **8**, or **16** bytes, as specified in the field description. If any other value (e.g., **128**) is entered, the application should display a validation error and prevent the user from proceeding to the next step.

tickets.summary: Band dropdown allows unsupported band selection for Mobility = true and FDD
tickets.description:
I observed that in the **Cell** section, when **Mobility** is set to **true** and **Duplex Mode** is set to **FDD**, the **Band** dropdown allows selecting **n34**. However, after selecting **n34** and proceeding, the following validation error is displayed:

> **\[CellConfig\] "Band": value must be one of "n1", "n2", "n3", "n5", "n7", "n8", "n12", "n13", "n14", "n18", "n20", "n24", "n25", "n26", "n28", "n30", "n66", "n70", "n71", "n74", "n85", "n91", "n92", "n93", "n94", "n100", "n105", "customBand" for SA profile 0.**

Since **n34** is not a valid band for this configuration, it should not be available in the **Band** dropdown. The UI currently allows selecting an unsupported value, which only fails during validation.

I also verified that when **Mobility** is set to **false** with **Duplex Mode = FDD**, the available band list is correct and does not exhibit this issue.

**Steps to Reproduce:**

1. Go to the **Cell** section.
2. Set **Mobility = true**.
3. Set **Duplex Mode = FDD**.
4. Open the **Band** dropdown and select **n34**.
5. Click **Next**.
6. Observe the validation error.

**Expected Result:**  
The **Band** dropdown should display only the supported bands for **Mobility = true** and **Duplex Mode = FDD**. Unsupported bands such as **n34** should not be available for selection.

tickets.summary: Custom Band - DL Frequency Min accepts invalid value with trailing '-' and clears the field on navigation
tickets.description:
**Description:**

In cell section, the **DL Frequency Min** field under **Custom Band** accepts an invalid value containing a trailing hyphen (e.g., `23-`) without displaying any validation error. After navigating to the next section and returning to the **Cell** section, the field is automatically cleared.

**Steps to Reproduce:**

1. Go to **Cell →Band -> Custom Band**.
2. Enter `23-` in the **DL Frequency Min** field.
3. Observe that no validation error is displayed.
4. Click **Next** to navigate to the next section.
5. Navigate back to the **Cell** section.
6. Observe that the **DL Frequency Min** field is blank.

**Actual Result:**  
The invalid value is accepted without validation, and the field is cleared when navigating back.

**Expected Result:**  
The application should immediately display a validation error for invalid input (e.g., `23-`) and should not allow navigation until the input is corrected. The field should not silently clear the entered value.

tickets.summary: Standardize the naming of the Export/Download action across the UI
tickets.description:
The application uses different labels for the same functionality. The bulk action toolbar displays **Export**, while the quick action menu displays **Download**. Using different terminology for the same action may cause confusion. The labels should be standardized for consistency throughout the application.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Open **My Tests**.
2. Select a test case using the checkbox and observe the bottom toolbar (**Export** option).
3. Hover over the same test case and observe the quick action toolbar (**Download** option).
4. Compare the action names.

tickets.summary: My Test: 'Date Modified' and 'Date Executed' filters return incorrect results for 'Between' and 'After' conditions
tickets.description:
**Step1:** Log in to Simnovator.

**Step2:** Navigate to the **My Test** page.

**Step3:** Click the **Filter** dropdown and add **Date Modified** and **Date Executed** from **Add Filter Fields**.

**Step4:** For the **Date Modified** filter, apply the **After** condition and verify the filtered results.

**Step5:** Change the filter condition to **Between**, select a valid date range, and verify the filtered results.

**Step6:** Repeat Steps 4 and 5 for the **Date Executed** filter. Observe the displayed test cases.

**Observed Result**

The **Date Modified** and **Date Executed** filters do not return the expected test cases when the **After** or **Between** filter conditions are applied. The filtered results do not accurately match the selected date criteria.

tickets.summary: Imported test case contains unexpected null values and extra iPerf profiles in traffic configuration.
tickets.description:
**Step1:** Log in to Simnovator.

**Step2:** On the **My Test** page, click **Import** from the top-right corner and import the test case provided by the customer.

**Step3:** After the test case is imported successfully, click **View** to open the imported test case.

**Step4:** Compare all sections of the imported test case with the original downloaded test case.

**Step5:** Navigate to the **Traffic** section and observe the imported configuration.

**Observed Result**

The imported test case does not match the original configuration. The **Traffic** section contains unexpected null values, and the imported test case includes **four iPerf profiles**, resulting in an incorrect traffic configuration.

tickets.summary: Log viewer fails to filter RNTI values using the 'between' operator.
tickets.description:
**Step1:** Log in to Simnovator.

**Step2:** Navigate to the **Logs** section and load logs using either of the following methods:

·        From the top-left corner, select any test case and the appropriate timestamp to load the logs.

·        **OR** enable **Offline Mode** from the top-right corner, click **Import Logs** from the top-left corner and wait until the logs are imported successfully.

**Step3:** Open the **Layer** filter and select the **PHY** layer.

**Step4:** Click **+ More Filters**, then click **+ Add** and add the **RNTI** filter from the available filter fields.

**Step5:** Open the **RNTI** filter, apply the **Between** operator by specifying a valid RNTI range and observe the filtered log entries.

**Step6:** Verify whether the displayed RNTI values fall within the specified range.

The Simnovator GUI fails to filter log entries correctly when the **RNTI** filter is applied using the **Between** operator. Log entries outside the specified RNTI range are displayed, or valid entries within the range are not returned.

tickets.summary: Incorrect time shown in the exported log

tickets.summary: User plane permits new data type addition despite incomplete mandatory fields.
tickets.description:
**Step1:** Log in to Simnovator.

**Step2:** On the **My Test** page, click **+ Create Test Case** from the top-right corner. The application navigates to the **Cell** page.

**Step3:** Select any **RAT**, then proceed to the **Subscriber** section and navigate to the **User Plane** section.

**Step4:** In the **User Plane** section:

o   Add **User Plane 1** and select the **Ping** data type.

o   Add **User Plane 2** and select the **HTTP** data type.

o   Leave the mandatory fields for the **HTTP** data type empty.

o   Click **+** to add **User Plane 3**.

o   Repeat the same process to continue adding additional User Plane entries without completing the mandatory fields of the previous entries.

**Step5:** Observe the behaviour.

**Observed Result**

The Simnovator GUI allows users to continuously add new User Plane data type entries even when one or more previously added entries have incomplete mandatory fields.

tickets.summary: Offline log viewer continues auto-scrolling after clicking "Jump to Latest".

tickets.summary: NB-IoT Subscriber AS Release Dropdown Displays Releases Above Release 14
tickets.description:
When **NB-IoT** is selected, the **AS Release** dropdown in the **Subscriber** section displays Release 15, Release 16, and Release 17. As per the expected product behavior, NB-IoT should support only LTE releases up to Release 14. Therefore, releases above Release 14 should not be available for selection.

**Steps to Reproduce:**

1. Open Test Creator.
2. In cell section, Select **RAT Type = NB-IoT**.
3. Navigate to the **Subscriber** section.
4. Open the **AS Release** dropdown.
5. Observe the available release options.

**Actual Result:**  
The AS Release dropdown displays Release 13, Release 14, Release 15, Release 16, and Release 17.

**Expected Result:**  
The AS Release dropdown should display only Release 13 and Release 14.

The Global Statistics file is downloaded successfully, but no success notification is displayed

tickets.summary: File Transfer Data field is cleared when changing Action from Uplink to Downlink/Both in IPERF User Plane
tickets.description:

7. Change **File Transfer Action** to **Downlink** and observe that the **Data Bitrate** field is no longer displayed.

tickets.summary: Global Statistics allows applying an unavailable Quick Range without validation
tickets.description:
I observed that when a test case is executed for approximately **150 seconds (3 minutes)**, the **Global Statistics → Settings → Quick Range** allows selecting **Last 10m** and clicking **Apply Changes**. Since only 3 minutes of execution data is available, the selected time range is not applicable. However, the application allows the selection without displaying any validation or visual indication.

### **Steps to Reproduce**

1. Execute a test case for approximately **150 seconds (3 minutes)**.
2. Open **Global Statistics**.
3. Click **Settings**.
4. Select **Quick Range → Last 10m**.
5. Click **Apply Changes**.
6. Observe the behavior.

### **Actual Result**

The application allows the user to select and apply **Last 10m** even though only 3 minutes of data is available. No validation message or visual indication is displayed.

### **Expected Result**

If the selected Quick Range is not applicable due to insufficient execution data, the application should:

* Disable the option or prevent it from being applied (e.g., display a **🚫** icon), **or**
* Display an informative validation message indicating that the selected time range is unavailable.

tickets.summary: Spectrum Analyzer: GUI does not display proper status or error message when spectrum view request fails.

**Actual Result:**

tickets.description:
**Step 1:** Log in to **Simnovator**.

**Step 2:** Navigate to the **My Test** page and click **+ Create Test Case** from the top-right corner. This redirects to the **Cell** configuration page.

**Step 3:** Select any **RAT** and proceed to the **Subscriber** section. Set the **PDN Type** to **IPv6**, then navigate to the **User Plane** section.

**Step 4:** In the **User Plane** section:

·        Select **Data Type = FTP**.

·        Enter the mandatory values for **File to Upload** and **File to Download**.

·        Enter the following valid compressed IPv6 address in the **Destination IP Address** field:  
2001:468:2000:1::

**Step 5:** Observe that Simnovator GUI rejects the valid compressed IPv6 address (2001:468:2000:1::) and displays an **"Invalid IP Address"** validation error. The field only accepts the fully expanded IPv6 format (e.g., 2001:468:2000:1:0:0:0:0).

tickets.summary: Expanded floating widget content is not fully visible when the widget is positioned at the bottom of the screen
tickets.description:
When the floating bubble is moved to the bottom of the page and the widget is expanded, part of the expanded widget content is hidden or clipped, making it difficult or impossible to view the complete information and access all controls. The widget should automatically reposition itself or adjust its expansion direction to ensure the entire content remains visible within the viewport.

### **Steps to Reproduce**

1. Open the application.
2. Drag the floating bubble to the bottom of the screen.
3. Expand the floating widget.
4. Observe the expanded widget content.  

    ![](blob:https://media.staging.atl-paas.net/?type=file&localId=08f3df8d84ff&id=67f728e5-4d55-46ea-86a7-42b4609310aa&&collection=&height=964&occurrenceKey=null&width=1916&__contextId=null&__displayType=null&__external=false&__fileMimeType=null&__fileName=null&__fileSize=null&__mediaTraceId=null&url=null)

tickets.summary: Log Message Details panel height shrinks based on filtered log count, impacting readability.
tickets.description:
**Step1:** Log in to **Simnovator**.

**Step2:** Navigate to the **Logs** section.

**Step3:** From the top-left corner, select any test case and its corresponding execution timestamp to load the logs.

**Step4:** Expand any log filter that contains only a few log messages.

**Step5:** Click on any filtered log message to open the **Log Message Details** panel.

**Step6:** Observe the size of the **Log Message Details** panel.

**Actual Result**

The **Log Message Details** panel height is reduced based on the number of filtered log messages. As a result, the panel becomes too small, making it difficult to view and analyse the complete log message content.

tickets.summary: 'View Report' option is unavailable for test cases with the Error verdict
tickets.description:
I observed that test cases with **Passed** and **Failed** verdicts provide a **View Report** option, allowing users to review execution details and verdict information.

However, for test cases with the **Error** verdict, the **View Report** option is not available. As a result, users cannot access the execution details or identify the reason for the error, making troubleshooting difficult.

### **Steps to Reproduce**

1. Execute a test case that completes with the **Passed** verdict.
2. Verify that the **View Report** option is available.
3. Execute a test case that completes with the **Failed** verdict.
4. Verify that the **View Report** option is available.
5. Execute a test case that completes with the **Error** verdict.
6. Observe the available actions.

![](blob:https://media.staging.atl-paas.net/?type=file&localId=9613b844b433&id=ead32eed-4dcd-451a-bb11-ff41a31ceaf4&&collection=&height=964&occurrenceKey=null&width=1914&__contextId=null&__displayType=null&__external=false&__fileMimeType=null&__fileName=null&__fileSize=null&__mediaTraceId=null&url=null)

tickets.summary: "Group By" filter does not display the selected option with a check mark on the My Test page.
tickets.description:
**Step1:** Log in to **Simnovator**.

**Step2:** Navigate to the **My Test** page.

**Step3:** Open any filter (e.g., **Status**, **Simulator**, **Verdict**, etc.), excluding **Group By**, and select an option.

**Step4:** Open the same filter again and observe that the selected option is displayed with a **check mark**, indicating the applied filter.

**Step5:** Open the **Group By** filter and select any grouping option.

**Step6:** Open the **Group By** filter again and observe that the selected option is **not** displayed with a check mark.

**Actual Result**

The **Group By** filter does not display a check mark next to the selected option after it is applied. As a result, users cannot easily identify the currently selected grouping option, whereas all other filters correctly indicate the selected option with a check mark.

tickets.summary: Inconsistent Graph type behaviour between expanded and collapsed KPI graphs.
tickets.description:
**Step 1:** Log in to **Simnovator**.

**Step 2:** Navigate to **Global Statistics**.

**Step 3:** Click the **three-dot (⋮) menu** on any KPI graph and select **Area Chart**.

**Step 4:** Expand the same KPI graph and observe that the graph reverts to the **Line Chart** instead of retaining the selected **Area Chart**.

**Step 5:** Collapse the graph again and observe that it is displayed correctly as an **Area Chart**.

**Step 6:** Repeat the same scenario in reverse:

·        Expand any KPI graph.

·        Change the graph type to **Area Chart**.

·        Collapse the graph.

**Step 7:** Observe that the collapsed graph reverts to the **Line Chart**. Expand the graph again and observe that the previously selected **Area Chart** is no longer applied.

**Actual Result**

The selected graph type is not synchronized between the **expanded** and **collapsed** views. The graph reverts to the default **Line Chart** when switching views, resulting in inconsistent behaviour.

tickets.summary: Graph tooltip overlaps chart data instead of positioning in available space
tickets.description:
I observed that when hovering over the graph, the tooltip displaying the timestamp and metric values appears directly over the plotted data. As a result, it obscures the graph, making it difficult for users to view the underlying trend or data points.

The tooltip should dynamically reposition itself to an area with sufficient empty space within the graph container so that it does not hide the graph. This behavior should be consistent even when the graph is expanded to full-screen.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Navigate to the **Global Statistics** page.
2. Hover over any data point in the **Packets/Sec** graph (or any graph with tooltips).
3. Observe the position of the tooltip while viewing the graph.
4. Expand the graph to full-screen and hover over the data points again.
5. Verify whether the tooltip overlaps and hides the graph data even when there is available empty space for positioning.

    ![](blob:https://media.staging.atl-paas.net/?type=file&localId=387c78d74341&id=da3bedc6-4a4f-4edd-bccd-d962422f3ba6&&collection=&height=968&occurrenceKey=null&width=1906&__contextId=null&__displayType=null&__external=false&__fileMimeType=null&__fileName=null&__fileSize=null&__mediaTraceId=null&url=null)

tickets.summary: Progress widget fails to update to 100% after Long-Run test completion.
tickets.description:
**Step1:** Log in to **Simnovator**.

**Step2:** Start any **long-duration test case** with **Log Settings** enabled.

**Step3:** Wait for the test case to complete.

**Step4:** Observe the **test status**, **verdict**, and the **progress widget**.

**Step5:** Notice that the test status is displayed as **Completed**, but the progress widget still shows **99% Completed**.

**Step6:** Refresh the browser and observe that the progress widget continues to display **99%**.

**Step7:** Open Simnovator in another browser (e.g., Chrome or Edge) and navigate to the same test execution.

**Step8:** Observe that the progress widget correctly displays **100% Completed**.

**Actual Result**

The test execution status is shown as **Completed**, but the progress widget remains at **99%** in the current browser session, even after refreshing the page. When the same test execution is opened in a different browser, the widget correctly displays **100% Completed**.

tickets.summary: Users cannot identify end of log list due to hidden scrollbar.

o   Alternatively, enable **Offline** mode from the top-right corner and import a log file using the **Import Logs** option.

**Step5:** Continuously press **PgUp** or **PgDn** to navigate through the log messages.

**Actual Result**

When the **Log Message Details** panel is open, it obscures the main log scrollbar. During **PgUp/PgDn** navigation, users cannot determine whether they have reached the first or last log entry because the scrollbar is not visible.

tickets.summary: All log layers are displayed despite specific log settings being applied.
tickets.description:
**Step1:** Log in to **Simnovator**.

**Step2:** Start any **long-duration test case** with specific **Log Settings** enabled (e.g., **rrc_debug** and **nas_rrc_debug**).

**Step3:** Navigate to the **Logs** section and monitor the generated logs.

**Step4:** Open the **Log Settings** dialog from the Logs page and verify that the configured log settings are displayed correctly.

**Step5:** Observe the logs displayed in the log viewer.

**Step6:** Notice that the log viewer displays log messages from **all layers** instead of only the layers configured in the applied log settings.

**Actual Result**

The **Log Settings** dialog correctly reflects the configured log settings (e.g., **rrc_debug** and **nas_rrc_debug**). However, the **Logs** page displays log messages from all layers rather than restricting the output to the configured log settings.

tickets.summary: Log viewer does not display logs for updated log settings until page refresh.

tickets.summary: Default Setting Option for Log Setting
tickets.description:
Currently, the **Success Setting** provides a star icon that allows the user to identify/set a configuration as the default setting. The **Log Setting** does not have a similar option.

To maintain consistency and provide the same functionality, the **Log Setting** should also support a default setting option using the star icon.

**Implementation Requirement:**

* Add a **star icon** to the Log Setting configuration, similar to Success Setting.
* Allow the user to select a Log Setting as the **default setting**.
* Clearly indicate the currently selected default Log Setting using the star icon.
* Maintain the same behavior and UI pattern used for the Success Setting.

**Expected Result:**  
Log Setting should have a default-setting option consistent with the existing Success Setting functionality.

tickets.summary: Enhancements requests for Bulk executions and Contextual controls
tickets.description:
**Current Implementation:**  
        Apex Scalable setup supports multiple testcase execution at a time but 

1. **No Parallel Execution:** Users cannot trigger multiple selected test cases to run concurrently.
2. **No Sequential Execution:** Users cannot select a batch of test cases and queue them to run automatically one after another, forcing tedious manual intervention after each individual test finishes.

**Proposed Implementation:**

When two or more test cases are selected, display a floating context bar at the top of the pane. Once execution begins, the menu morphs to provide specific stop and control handles depending on the chosen run mode:

* **Before Execution Starts:**

    * `▶ Run Parallel (Simultaneous)` — Launches all selected items at once.
    * `🔢▶ Run Sequential (Queued)` — Initializes an automated top-to-bottom queue.
    
* **After execution starts** 

**Parallel Execution Mode:**

* `⏹ Stop All Active/Stop Selected testcase` — Sends a graceful termination signal (e.g., `SIGTERM`) to all running test threads so they can safely write logs, save PCAP files, and exit cleanly without data corruption.

 **Sequential Execution Mode:**

* `⏹ Stop Current & Pause` — Gracefully terminates the single active test case currently executing and pauses the pipeline. The remaining test cases stay locked in their `Queued / Waiting` state so an operator can fix a lab issue and click `▶ Resume Queue`.
* `⏭ Skip Current` — Instantly stops the active test case, marks its status badge as `Skipped`, and immediately triggers the initialization script for the next test case waiting in line.
* `❌ Clear Remaining Queue` — Keeps the current active test running to completion but instantly flushes all upcoming test cases out of the execution line, returning their row checkboxes to an idle state.

tickets.summary: [SpaceX] Logs endpoint time window is second-granular and inclusive on both ends — paging loses or duplicates log records
tickets.description:
Raised from SD-4136 (SpaceX, Alex Mahlon, 12 Aug 2026).

`GET /v2/testcases/executions/{executionId}/logs` takes `startTime` and `endTime` in unix seconds, but log entries are timestamped in microseconds and the range looks inclusive at both ends. So there is no way to page through logs without either dropping records or repeating them:

* `[0,5]` then `[6,10]` loses everything in (5s, 6s)
* `[0,5]` then `[5,10]` repeats anything at exactly 5s

Fine for the stats endpoints, which take the same parameters but sample at 1 Hz. Not fine for logs.

Already flagged internally: the API YAML gap audit (v3.0.0, 29 May 2026) raised the same seconds vs microseconds mismatch as C13 and C14, spec lines 1714 and 1720. The inclusive/exclusive behaviour itself is undocumented, so it needs confirming against a build before we commit. QA script is ready to run on the .95 rack.

**Fix:** make the window half-open, with both parameters treated as exact microsecond instants.

```
startTime * 1_000_000  <=  ts  <  endTime * 1_000_000
```

Windows then tile exactly. `[0,4)` and `[4,8)` return every record once, and data at 4.3s falls in the second window. Sub-second parameters are not needed to fix this.

Breaking change for anyone relying on the current inclusive end, they silently lose their last record. Needs a version note before it ships.

tickets.summary: [SpaceX] Add counters to UE / Cell / Global statistics endpoints
tickets.description:
Raised from SD-4135 (SpaceX, Daniel Lampie, 12 Aug 2026).

Customer wants extra counters exposed on the v2 statistics endpoints.

**UE stats** - `/v2/testcases/executions/{executionId}/statistics/ues`
RACH counter, RLF counter, average TX power, handover attempts/successes, voice call active flag, voice call RTP packet loss.

**Cell stats** - `/v2/testcases/executions/{executionId}/statistics/cells`
RRC active UEs, RRC idle UEs, handover attempts/successes, RLF counter, active voice calls.

**Global stats** - `/v2/testcases/executions/{executionId}/statistics/global`
Per-cell breakdown (or fold it into cell stats), and 1 second granularity to match UE and Cell stats.

Notes:

* The customer titled the ticket "Enhance Logging Fields" but all three are statistics endpoints, nothing to do with the logger.
* The global stats item is a different kind of ask to the rest. UE and Cell already do 1s granularity, so that one is an inconsistency between sibling endpoints rather than new data, and can probably ship on its own.
* Check overlap with SIM40-2738 (NAS/RRC counters for validation) before starting. Similar counters, different consumer.

tickets.summary: Power ON Duration Validation and Error Message Are Incorrect
tickets.description:
The validation for **Power ON Duration (sec)** appears to consider both **Start Delay** and **Duration**. However, the error message labels the calculated value as only **Duration**, which is misleading.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Set **Start Delay** to `10` seconds.
2. Set **Duration** to `600` seconds.
3. Enter a **Power ON Duration** value less than `615` seconds, for example `606` seconds.

![](blob:https://media.staging.atl-paas.net/?type=file&localId=4ccecdcf2d38&id=32b9b207-dd18-4291-bc41-061ccb4251b2&&collection=&height=992&occurrenceKey=null&width=1910&__contextId=null&__displayType=null&__external=false&__fileMimeType=null&__fileName=null&__fileSize=null&__mediaTraceId=null&url=null)
### Actual Result

The following error message is displayed:

> **Power On Time should be at least 5 seconds greater than Duration. (Duration: 610)**

The value `610` is displayed as **Duration**, even though the configured Duration is only `600` seconds.

Based on the validation behavior, the calculation appears to be:

`Start Delay (10) + Duration (600) = 610 seconds`

Therefore, the minimum required Power ON Duration is:

`610 + 5 = 615 seconds`

### Expected Result

The error message should clearly indicate that the validation is based on the sum of **Start Delay + Duration**, rather than displaying the calculated value as only Duration.

For example:

> **Power ON Duration should be at least 5 seconds greater than the total of Start Delay and Duration. (Start Delay + Duration: 610 seconds)**

tickets.summary: Total Test Duration Validation Message Does Not Include Ramp-up Offset
tickets.description:
## Steps to Reproduce

1. Go to the **User Plane** configuration.
2. Set the **Data Type** to **No Data**, Go to the **Traffic** configuration.
3. Set the **Loop Profile** to **Time Based**.
4. Set **Power ON Duration** to **650 seconds**.
5. Set **Power OFF Duration** to **5 seconds**.
6. Enter **655 seconds** as the **Total Test Duration**.
7. Click **Next**.
8. Observe that the system displays an error requiring **656 seconds**, including the Ramp-up Offset.

Initially, the system displays:

**“Total Test Duration should be at least equal to the total time taken for all power on/off cycles. (Minimum: 655s)”**

Based on this message, I entered **655 seconds** as the Total Test Duration and clicked **Next**.

However, the system then displays the following error:

**“\[PowerCycleConfig\] Total Test Duration should be at least Power On Time + Power Off Time + Ramp-up offset for profile 0. Minimum: 656.00”**

The initial validation message does not include the **Ramp-up Offset**, causing a mismatch between the displayed minimum duration and the actual validation requirement.  
  
**Expected message:**

“Total Test Duration should be at least 656 seconds to accommodate all Power ON/OFF cycles and the required UE startup time.”

tickets.summary: Logs Section: Unable to Filter “-” Values in UE ID and Cell ID Filters
tickets.description:
For the **DIR** filter, the value **“-”** is available in the dropdown, so users can select it and filter the corresponding log entries.

However, for the **UE ID** and **Cell ID** filters, some log entries contain **“-”**, but the **“-”** option is not available in their respective filter dropdowns. Because of this, users are unable to specifically filter and view the log entries where the **UE ID** or **Cell ID** value is **“-”**.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Navigate to the **Logs** section.
2. Check the log entries containing **“-”** values.
3. Open the **DIR** filter dropdown and observe that **“-”** is available as a filter option.
4. Open the **UE ID** and **Cell ID** filter dropdowns.
5. Observe that **“-”** is not available as a filter option, even though logs containing this value are displayed.

## Actual Result

The **DIR** filter allows users to filter log entries with the value **“-”**, but the **UE ID** and **Cell ID** filters do not provide the **“-”** option. Therefore, users cannot filter and view the corresponding log entries.

## Expected Result

If **“-”** is displayed as a value in the log entries, it should also be available as a filter option for the corresponding fields, including **UE ID** and **Cell ID**, so users can filter those log entries properly.

**Step 3:** Once the test case is started, navigate to **UE Statistics** and monitor the **Bitrate (DL) Mbps** and **Bitrate (UL) Mbps** values.

**Step 4:** Observe the **Bitrate (UL) Mbps** value.

**Observation:**  
Simnovator GUI displays the **UL Bitrate as 0 Mbps** for low bitrate values.

tickets.summary: Blocker for Multi-RAT testing: configuration throws CIOTOpt missing property error when UE groups are assigned to different serving cells
tickets.description:
When the **RAT Type** is configured as **Multi-RAT** in the **Cell** section, an error is observed in the **Subscriber** section when different UE groups are assigned to different serving cells.

The issue occurs only when **UE Group 0 and UE Group 1 are assigned to different serving cells**.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Create a new test case.
2. Navigate to the **Cell** section.
3. Set the **RAT Type** to **Multi-RAT**.
4. Click **Next** to proceed to the **Subscriber** section.
5. In the Subscriber section:

    * For **UE Group 0**, select **Serving Cell = Cell 0**.
    * For **UE Group 1**, select **Serving Cell = Cell 1**.
    
6. Click **Next**.
7. Observe the error message displayed.

## Actual Result

A popup error message is displayed:

`[SubsConfig]: missing properties: 'CIOTOpt' for MULTIRAT 4G profile 1`

The user is unable to proceed because the subscriber configuration validation fails.

## Comparison / Additional Observation

If both UE groups are assigned to the **same serving cell**, the error does not occur.

For example:

* **UE Group 0 → Serving Cell 0**
* **UE Group 1 → Serving Cell 0**

In this configuration, clicking **Next** proceeds without displaying the `CIOTOpt` error.

However, when the serving cells are different:

* **UE Group 0 → Serving Cell 0**
* **UE Group 1 → Serving Cell 1**

the following error is displayed:

`[SubsConfig]: missing properties: 'CIOTOpt' for MULTIRAT 4G profile 1`

tickets.summary: License expiry verification fails during initial testbed preparation after configuration soft-link and LTE restart
tickets.description:
While preparing the testbed, an issue is observed during the initial LTE service restart after soft-linking the configuration file.

After soft-linking the required configuration file, when `service lte restart` is executed for the first time, the testbed preparation fails with the following error:

> **Preparing the Testbed**  
> **Could not verify license expiry: Network time source unreachable; please try again.**

The error occurs during the license expiry verification step, indicating that the network time source could not be reached at that time.

When the same command, `service lte restart`, is executed again, the issue is resolved. The testbed preparation then proceeds successfully without showing the license expiry/network time source error.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Prepare the testbed setup.
2. Soft-link the required configuration file.
3. Execute:  
  `service lte restart`
4. Start/continue the testbed preparation process.
5. Observe the error during the license expiry verification.
6. Execute `service lte restart` again.
7. Continue the testbed preparation.

### Actual Result

During the first LTE service restart, the testbed preparation fails with:

**“Could not verify license expiry: Network time source unreachable; please try again.”**

A second `service lte restart` is required to resolve the issue, after which the testbed preparation works as expected.

### Expected Result

After soft-linking the configuration file and performing `service lte restart`, the network time source should be available and the license expiry should be verified successfully on the first attempt.

The user should not need to restart the LTE service a second time to proceed with testbed preparation.

tickets.summary: Power On Time Validation Message Is Incorrect When Loop Is Enabled
tickets.description:
When **Loop** is enabled, the Power On Time validation message is not displayed correctly.

The current message is:

> **“When loop is enabled, Power On Time should be at least 5 seconds greater than Duration + Start Delay (3110)”**

The message indicates that the Power On Time should be at least **5 seconds greater than Duration + Start Delay**, and displays **3110** as the reference value. However, this does not clearly represent the expected Power On Time considering the loop configuration.

**Steps to Reproduce:**

1. Enable **Loop**.
2. Configure the required Duration, Start Delay, No. of Loops, and Inter-Loop Interval.
3. Enter a Power On Time that does not satisfy the validation condition.
4. Observe the validation message displayed.

**Actual Result:**

The validation message is displayed as:

**“When loop is enabled, Power On Time should be at least 5 seconds greater than Duration + Start Delay (3110)”**

The message does not clearly/accurately communicate the expected Power On Time based on the configured loop parameters.

**Expected Result:**

The validation message should clearly display the **actual minimum required Power On Time** based on the configured Start Delay, Duration, No. of Loops, and Inter-Loop Interval.

The message should also clearly explain the calculation used to derive the minimum required Power On Time.

tickets.summary: User Plane loop is not working when Traffic loop is Enabled

Steps to Reproduce:

2. Create any testcase by configuring Data type as Iperf and enable the user Plane Loop(Duration: 30secs, loop count-3, Interloop - 10secs) and also enable the Traffic loop (count based - 2, Power ON: 130secs).
3. Execute this testcase and go to global statistics
4. Issue: Observe that throuhput is not coming up after the 1st user plane loop(30+10secs) is completed.

Please note that user plane loop is working when Traffic loop is not enabled  
  
Suspected Root cause: Iperf command is not started after 1st loop is completed (30+10 secs). When Traffic loop is enabled "loop_count" and "loop_delay" for iperf configuration in UE.CFG is updated same as traffic loop count and delay.

Suggested fix: Handle the loop_delay and loop_count for User Plane and Traffic separately in UE configuration file.

tickets.summary: Sync Test Case Status and Add Verdict in Dashboard Recent Activities
tickets.description:
There are two improvements required in **Dashboard → Recent Activities**:

1. **Display the correct Test Case Status**

* In **My Tests**, when a test case is executed, its Status is displayed as **In Progress**.
* However, in **Dashboard → Recent Activities**, the Status for the same test case is not displayed as **In Progress**.
* Recent Activities should fetch the current Status from **My Tests** and display the same value.
* For example, if the test case Status in My Tests is **In Progress**, the Status in Recent Activities should also be **In Progress** instead of `-`.

2. **Add Verdict to Recent Activities**

* In **My Tests**, the test case has a **Verdict** field.
* Currently, in **Dashboard → Recent Activities**, only the **Status** field is available; the **Verdict** field is not present.
* Add a **Verdict** field to Recent Activities.
* The Verdict should be fetched from the corresponding test case in **My Tests** and displayed in Recent Activities.

**Expected Result:**

Dashboard → Recent Activities should show the same current **Status** as My Tests and should additionally provide the **Verdict** information for each test case.

tickets.summary: Unable to Execute 2-Cell/3-Cell Test Case When 3 SDRs Are Assigned to a User
tickets.description:
When an admin assigns **3 SDRs to a user**, the user is unable to execute a **2-cell or 3-cell test case** using the assigned SDR resources.

The test execution starts and the UE process is launched, but the UE fails during the **PCIe synchronization/calibration phase**. As a result, the RF driver cannot be initialized and the test execution is aborted.

### **Steps to Reproduce**

1. Login as **Admin**.
2. Assign **3 SDRs** to a user.
3. Login with the assigned user.
4. Create/select a **2-cell or 3-cell test case** that requires the assigned SDRs.
5. Start the test case execution.
6. Observe the UE/terminal logs during UE startup.

### **Actual Result**

The UE fails during PCIe synchronization/calibration and the test cannot proceed.

The following errors are observed in the UE logs:

```
Starting PCIe Sync...
PCIe Calibration started
sdr=/dev/sdr0 PCIe Calibration Failed 1
Could set RF driver start params
```

The UE process then exits instead of successfully initializing the RF driver.

The recording also shows the test case execution being **aborted/incomplete** from the Simnovator UI.

### **Expected Result**

When **3 SDRs are assigned to the user**, the user should be able to execute supported **2-cell and 3-cell test cases** successfully.

The assigned SDRs should be correctly detected and initialized, PCIe synchronization/calibration should complete successfully, and the UE/RF driver should start without errors.

**Step5:** Increase the UE count beyond **10 UEs per UE Group** and observe the behaviour.

**Step6:** Check the RRC logs for the affected UEs.

## Actual Result

* Simnovator fails to register all UEs when the UE count exceeds **10 UEs per UE Group**.
* Throughput is not established for all UEs.
* The following RRC message is observed:

```
Cell is not suitable
pci=500 arfcn=633984 rsrp=-88.8 rsrq=-21.8
q_rxlev_min=-70 q_qual_min=-20
Srxlev=51.2 Squal=-1.8
```

* **PDCP and RLC re-establishment** is also observed for affected UEs.

tickets.summary: Test Case Verdict lacks detailed breakdown and counts for specific NAS/RRC failure messages
tickets.description:
Steps to Reproduce:

1. Login to Simnovator
2. Execute any failure scenario testcases to get any RRC/NAS reject messages. (Create new Success criteria as Message counters-->ALL NAS or ALL RRC Failures)
3. Let's wait for testcase completion and click the verdict. 
4. Observe that it shows only Metric -  all_nas_failures and measured 5 (for example).

Issue: 

Issue Summary  
The Test Case verdict provides a high-level verdict (FAIL) based on an aggregate metric (all_nas_failures < 1), but it does not expose the specific message required for debugging.  
Key Problems:

* Missing Details: It lacks visibility into which exact Non-Access Stratum (NAS) or Radio Resource Control (RRC) messages (e.g., Attach Reject, Authentication Reject, Service Reject) triggered the failure.
* Incorrect Metric unit for Message counter: The Measured Unit shows percentage though it is displaying the actual count, which leads to confusion for the user.

tickets.summary: Global Statistics displays current test execution instead of last test result.

tickets.summary: Incomplete RRC signalling messages and missing NAS Layer in Simnovator offline logs after import.

tickets.summary: IPv6 Address Not Displayed in UE Statistics When Using IPv4v6 Configuration

tickets.summary: Inconsistent resource configuration behaviour during ongoing test execution.
tickets.description:
**Step 1:** Log in to Simnovator using any valid user account.

**Step 2:** Navigate to the **My Test** page and start any test case on User 1.

**Step 3:** Once the test case is running, open another browser session and log in as an administrator. Verify that the application redirects to the Tools page.

**Step 4:** Navigate to **Tools → Simnovator Management → Manage Simulator** to open the Simulator Management page.

**Step 5:** Under the Container Hosts section, click **Details** for each user and verify the assigned SDR cards under the RF Card section.

**Step 6:** From the Details panel, open the License section and check the Max UE per Instance value for each user.

**Step 7:** Verify that User 2 and User 3 do not have any SDR cards assigned and that the SDR card pairs SDR2–SDR3 and SDR4–SDR5 are available for assignment.

**Step 8:** Open the Details panel for User 1, on which the test case is currently running. Under the RF Card section, attempt to assign either of the available SDR card pairs (SDR2–SDR3 or SDR4–SDR5).

**Step 9:** Observe that the available SDR card options are grayed out and cannot be assigned to User 1 while the test case is running.

**Step 10:** In the same Details panel, navigate to the License section and open the License Server panel. Change the Max UE per Instance value from 1000 to 1200 and click Save.

**Step 11:** Verify that the updated value is displayed in the License section.

**Step 12:** Return to the Simulator Management page and reopen the Details panel for User 1 while the test case is still running.

**Step 13:** Verify that the updated Max UE per Instance value of 1200 is reflected for User 1, even though SDR card assignment remains unavailable during the ongoing test execution.

**Actual Result:**

During an ongoing test execution, the administrator can update the Max UE per Instance license value, and the updated value is successfully reflected for the user running the test case.

However, the administrator cannot assign available SDR cards to the same user because the SDR card options are grayed out.

This demonstrates inconsistent behavior in resource configuration management, as the application allows UE license updates while restricting SDR card assignment for a user with an ongoing test execution.

tickets.summary: Cell-Wise Cell Type, Channel Bandwidth, and MIMO information not displayed correctly in NSA mobility scenario.
tickets.description:
**Step 1:** Log in to Simnovator using any valid user account.

**Step 2:** Create an **NSA Mobility test case** with the following cell configuration:

* **Cell 0:** Cell Type: 4G, Channel Bandwidth: 20 MHz, MIMO: 4 DL Antennas and 1 UL Antenna.
* **Cell 1:** Cell Type: 5G, Channel Bandwidth: 100 MHz, MIMO: 4 DL Antennas and 1 UL Antenna.
* **Cell 2:** Cell Type: 4G, Channel Bandwidth: 20 MHz, MIMO: 4 DL Antennas and 1 UL Antenna.

**Step 3:** Start the created test case.

**Step 4:** Navigate to the **My Test** page.

**Step 5:** Open the test case in either the **In Progress** or **Completed** state.

**Step 6:** Navigate to the **Test Case Information** section.

**Step 7:** Verify the displayed **Cell Type, Channel Bandwidth, and MIMO** information against the configuration defined during test case creation.

* **Cell Type:** The GUI displays `4G / 5G` instead of representing the cell types for all three cells as `4G / 5G / 4G`. The Cell Type configured for Cell 2 is not separately represented.
* **Channel Bandwidth:** The GUI displays `100 MHz / 20 MHz` instead of representing the configured bandwidth for all three cells as `20 MHz / 100 MHz / 20 MHz`. The bandwidth configured for Cell 0 is not separately represented.
* **MIMO:** The GUI displays `4×4 DL / 1×1 UL` instead of accurately representing the configured MIMO for all three cells as `4×1 / 4×1 / 4×1`. The displayed information does not clearly reflect the configured antenna counts for each cell, where each cell has 4 DL antennas and 1 UL antenna.

As a result, users cannot clearly identify the Cell Type, Channel Bandwidth, and MIMO configuration of each cell from the Test Case Information section.

**Step 1:** Log in to Simnovator as an Admin user.

**Step 2:** Navigate to **Simulator Management → Manage Simulator**. The Simulator Management page will be displayed.

**Step 3:** Under **Container Hosts**, click **Details** for each user to verify their assigned RF cards.

**Step 4:** Verify the RF card allocation for each user:

* **User1 (simuser):** sdr0, sdr1
* **User2 (Sruthi):** sdr2, sdr3
* **User3 (Mohan):** sdr4, sdr5

**Step 5:** Log in to Simnovator as **User1 (simuser)** in a separate session and start any test case using the assigned RF cards.

**Step 6:** While the test case is starting, switch to the Admin session and navigate to **Simulator Management → Manage Simulator**.

**Step 7:** Under **Container Hosts**, click **Details** for User1 (simuser) and remove the assigned RF cards (sdr0 and sdr1) while the test case is still ongoing.

### Actual Result

1. The test case takes a long time to start in the Simnovator GUI.
2. The Admin page displays **Not in use** for sdr0 and sdr1 under Container Hosts, even though the test case is still ongoing for User1 (simuser).
3. The Admin can assign sdr0 and sdr1 to another user while these RF cards are still being used by User1.
4. User1's Details panel shows no RF cards assigned after the Admin removes them, despite the ongoing test execution.

tickets.summary: Inconsistent Error Verdict Behavior and Empty Test Case Report in My Test Case and Global Stats
tickets.description:
When a test case execution has an **Error** verdict, the behavior is inconsistent between the My Test Case and Global Stats sections.

In the **My Test Case** section, clicking the Error verdict does not open the Test Case Report.

However, in the **Global Stats** section, clicking the Error verdict opens the Test Case Report page, but no report details are displayed.

The Error verdict behavior should be consistent across both sections. If a Test Case Report is available for an execution with an Error verdict, it should open and display the relevant report details. If no report is available, the application should handle the situation consistently in both sections without opening an empty report.

**Steps to Reproduce:**

1. Create and execute a test case.
2. Observe that the execution has an Error verdict.
3. Navigate to the **My Test Case** section and click the Error verdict.
4. Observe that the Test Case Report does not open.
5. Navigate to the **Global Stats** section and click the Error verdict.
6. Observe that the Test Case Report page opens, but no report details are displayed.

**Actual Result:**

* **My Test Case:** Clicking the Error verdict does not open the Test Case Report.
* **Global Stats:** Clicking the Error verdict opens the Test Case Report page, but the report is empty.

**Expected Result:**

* The Error verdict behavior must be consistent in both My Test Case and Global Stats.
* If an execution report exists, clicking the Error verdict should open the corresponding Test Case Report and display the available execution details, logs, and error information.
* If no report exists for an execution, the application should display an appropriate message instead of showing an empty report.
* The report must correspond to the selected test case execution.

tickets.summary: Admin unable to stop another User's ongoing test case or delete the user to release Simulator resources.
tickets.description:
**Step 1:** Log in to Simnovator using any valid user account.

**Step 2:** Navigate to the **My Test** page and start any long-duration test case.

**Step 3:** Log in to Simnovator using an Admin account in a separate session.

**Step 4:** Navigate to **Tools → Manage Simulator** under Simulator Management. The Simulator Management page will be displayed.

**Step 5:** Check whether any option is available for the Admin to stop the ongoing test case executed by another user. Observe that no such option is available.

**Step 6:** Navigate to **User Management** and attempt to delete the user whose test case is currently running so that the Admin can create another user and execute a new test case. Observe that Simnovator does not allow the Admin to delete the user while the test case is in progress.

### Actual Result

The Admin cannot stop another user's ongoing test case or delete the associated user while the test case is running. Consequently, the Admin cannot create another user to execute a new test case on the occupied setup and must wait until the existing user manually stops the test case or its execution completes.
